Record where a CATLAS raw-data bundle came from

Source: R/rawdata-provenance.R
build_provenance.Rd

Constructor for the catlas_provenance class. Each data bundle carries a provenance record, allowing the data bundle object to answer when it was extracted, from where, which study it comes from, and which experiment build was used to collect the data.

Usage

build_provenance(
  study,
  design,
  blocks,
  trial_types,
  origin,
  collected_between = NULL,
  retrieved_at = Sys.time(),
  experiment_build,
  notes = character(),
  guided = FALSE
)

Arguments

study

Character(1). Study identifier of the form <prefix>-<task>-<mode>-0X. Its components are parsed, so for instance fba-allergy-online-01 yields prefix = "fba", task = "allergy", mode = "online", wave = 1L. See Details for further explanation of the naming convention.

design

Character(1). Structural variant of the procedure. Currently one of "three-stage-replication" or "three-stage-extension". See Details for explanation of supported study designs.

blocks

Named integer vector. Number of blocks per stage, named by stage exactly as trials$stage is coded. For instance, the three-stage allergy of the forward-blocking-attention-01 manuscript supplies: c(stage1 = 10L, stage2 = 8L, stage3 = 6L, test = 6L).

trial_types

Integer(1). Distinct trial types presented per block, 8 for the three-stage allergy task. Together with blocks, the trial_types are used to derive the expected trial count.

origin

Named list comprising of platform (one of "JATOS", "Prolific", "OSF", "synthetic"), url, study_id and batch_ids. study_id may hold several IDs when the batches span more than one platform study, e.g. after a re-deployment.

collected_between

Named Date vector or a pair of strings as.Date() can parse, as c(first = , last = ). Records the first and last day on which the experiment was run. Required unless the platform is "synthetic". This field is not the same as retrieved_at. collected_between records when the experiment was run, retrieved_at when the data was imported.

retrieved_at

POSIXct(1) or a string parseable by as.POSIXct(). Coerced to UTC. Defaults to the current time.

experiment_build

Named list comprising of repo, release and commit. At least one of release and commit must be given unless the platform is "synthetic" (which refers to simulated, not collected data).

notes

Character. Free text.

guided

Logical(1). When TRUE, every other argument is ignored and the record is collected by prompting at the console, then the equivalent call is printed for pasting into a script. Requires an interactive session.

Value

A validated object of class "catlas_provenance".

Details

Naming conventions (study)

CATLAS uses a specific study naming convention that allows it to keep some order in the chaos that is scientific publishing. Each experiment must be named according to this convention, and thus be of the form <prefix>-<task>-<mode>-0X. In this study name, each components carries its own specific meaning:

  • <prefix> means study type or manuscript family. For instance, fba refers to forward-blocking-attention experiments aimed at illuminating the role attention plays in the forward blocking phenomenon in cue contingency learning.

  • <task> is a broad family to which task used by the experiment falls. It refers to the cover story, not to the formal structure of the experiment. For instance, allergy refers to the commonly used allergy prediction family of tasks.

  • <mode> refers to the data collection mode. Currently support online ("online"), behavioural on-site ("lab"), eye-tracking containing ("eye"), and electroencephalography containing ("eeg") data.

  • 0X is the wave indicating order of this experiment in a series of experiments from the same study type/manuscript family (<prefix>), using the same task variant (<task>), and collected via the same data collection method (<mode>). The order does NOT reset with each new manuscript and it is thus possible to have the first experiment of a manuscript containing wave number of more than one. The wave identifier 0X is coerced to integer via as.integer().

Supported study designs (design)

Study design parameter provides information about above and beyond what you put into study. Most importantly, while the <task> field of study informs about the experiment's "cover story," design reflects formal set-up and study procedure information. Currently, the following designs are supported:

  • three-stage-replication refers to a formally exact replication of the Beesley & Le Pelley's (2011) study which demonstrated that forward blocking in a three-stage cue-outcome contingency learning paradigm correlates with eye-tracking proxies of overt attention

  • three-stage-extension refers to a procedure reflecting Paskewitz & Jones's (2020) desing suggestion for adjudicating between attentional shift and attentional competition accounts of forward blocking within associability-based associative models of cue-outcome contingency learning

References

Beesley, T., & Le Pelley, M. E. (2011). The influence of blocking on overt attention and associability in human learning. Journal of Experimental Psychology: Animal Behavior Processes, 37(1), 114–120. doi:10.1037/a0019526

Paskewitz, S., & Jones, M. (2020). Dissecting EXIT. Journal of Mathematical Psychology*, 97, 102371. doi:10.1016/j.jmp.2020.102371

See also

build_fba_rawdata(), provenance(), record_exclusion()

Examples

build_provenance(
  study = "fba-allergy-online-01",
  design = "three-stage-replication",
  blocks = c(stage1 = 10L, stage2 = 8L, stage3 = 6L, test = 6L),
  trial_types = 8L,
  origin = list(
    platform = "JATOS",
    url = "https://jatos.mindprobe.eu",
    study_id = "catlas_01",
    batch_ids = c(30206L, 30275L, 30832L, 30829L)
  ),
  collected_between = c(
    first = as.Date("2026-06-09"),
    last  = as.Date("2026-06-26")
  ),
  retrieved_at = as.POSIXct("2026-06-26 12:00:00", tz = "UTC"),
  experiment_build = list(
    repo = "josefmana/catlaslab",
    release = "fba-allergy-online-01",
    commit = "e249e74"
  )
)

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Answer the prompts, then paste the printed call into data-raw/.
prov <- build_provenance(guided = TRUE)
} # }
